description: Fleet session-management Phase B, D1+D2 (§4). Validates role_class (ephemeral | project | principal — primary/chat are never spawn-assigned), work_class, and budget_line; when role_name is given, checks the fill-never-mint rule for principal offices (role_not_legislated when no role row exists yet) and the reserved <solet>-Main mint guard (reserved_role_name). Writes the managed_session ledger row in 'spawning' state BEFORE resolving and dispatching through the host driver, so a half-failed spawn stays visible rather than silently disappearing. Three host drivers ship: 'operator' (degenerate, observes via registration only, never spawns), 'headless' (D1 — spawns an actual Claude Code process over stream-json, config-gated fail-closed on a resolved permission mode/.mcp.json/the claude binary), and 'tmux' (D2 — spawns a detached tmux session running the interactive claude CLI, config-gated fail-closed on the tmux binary/version plus the same claude-launch checks as headless; its spawn() also runs a bounded PTY-confirm expect loop for the interactive --dangerously-load-development-channels prompt, fail-closed on timeout). Host choice affects deploy survival: a 'headless' worker is swap-mortal by construction (a direct child of the platform process, killed unconditionally on every platform stop including a blue-green deploy's quiesce step) while a 'tmux' worker is swap-durable by construction (its pane belongs to the independent tmux daemon, untouched by the platform's stop/swap path) — prefer 'tmux' for any worker expected to outlive a single release; a deploy holding live headless workers needs an explicit quiesce-or-accept decision recorded in the deploy reason. A spawn-time PreToolUse tool allowlist mechanism exists (allowed_tools, or resolved per_work_class from plugin.yaml's work_class_tool_allowlists) — an out-of-allowlist tool call is denied with a clean error, never executed and never a silent hang — but per operator ruling (2026-08-03, 'we don't have any restrictions now') it ships UNARMED by default: an empty/unconfigured allowlist means no extra restriction, not a lockdown. The permission mode itself (plugin.yaml's headless_permission_mode) similarly accepts any value today; the driver only refuses when no mode resolves at all. The tmux driver denies Claude Code's structured-choice AskUserQuestion tool by default (operator ruling, 2026-08-14 — its blocking picker stalls an unattended or peer-driven session); allow_askuserquestion=true lifts the deny for that one spawn. The headless driver needs no equivalent: measured live, its stream-json mode never enumerates the tool in the first place, so the flag is inert there. The codex runtime has no equivalent tool at all. W6 (#13 §44.3, 2026-08-14): local_name is the name the spawned worker answers to on its OWN machine — the headless driver's --name and the tmux driver's --name plus the label its session name derives from. Omitted, it defaults to role_name for a project-class role and to lane_id otherwise. Git-Controller is a project-class role, not a principal one: a `plugin::agent_messaging_plugin::provision_role_session` call with role_name='Git-Controller' and no requested_role_class resolves it to project and assigns local_name='Git-Controller'. This is what lets a spawned Git-Controller pass the git mutation guard IMMEDIATELY, on its first turn, instead of needing a second driven turn to claim its name first: the guard resolves its caller by reading the local session file's 'name' field and comparing it EXACTLY, so the worker has to be born with the right local name. Verified on both hosts. ROUTING IS A SEPARATE THING, and the distinction matters: passing the mutation guard does NOT make peer_send_by_name deliver to that role. Spawning deliberately does NOT claim the durable role binding (operator ruling, 2026-08-14) — claiming a role adds a name and never releases the incumbent's, so an automatic claim at spawn would EVICT whoever currently holds it: a destructive act triggered by a routine one. The spawned worker claims its role explicitly once it is up, and only then does role-addressed routing reach it. role_name is recorded on the ledger row as the spawn's stated INTENT, never as a claim. REFUSAL (operator ruling, 2026-08-14): a second spawn under a local_name that a non-terminal managed_session row already holds is refused loudly with local_name_already_held, naming the incumbent's agent_instance_id, lifecycle_state, host, host_ref and lane, plus the terminate_session call that would free the name. Never a silent uniquifying suffix — the guard's compare is exact, so 'Git-Controller-2' is simply a session that cannot mutate git — and never a silent eviction. The ordering is terminate the holder, THEN spawn the replacement. HOW THIS RELATES TO THE OTHER TWO ROLE GATES, since an adopter will meet these three in some order and reading only one of them teaches the wrong general rule: (1) THIS verb refuses a second spawn under a live local name; (2) peer_claim_role independently refuses a claim against a LIVE different-session holder with role_held_live, unless an explicit takeover is passed after operator confirmation — that gate already shipped and is NOT new here, so do not build a second one on top of it; (3) a holder that reads DEAD by the liveness window is claimable cheaply, with no explicit terminate, and this is deliberate rather than an oversight: a session that crashed can no longer release its own role, so a gate that also refused dead holders would strand that role permanently behind a session that no longer exists — a worse failure than the collision the refusal exists to prevent. Crash succession stays cheap on purpose. W4A (#8 §43.1, 2026-08-14): degraded_hooks_acknowledged (default false) is the explicit opt-in to spawn onto a host whose preflight can PROVE the worker's hooks will not run — a managed Claude Code policy listing 'hooks' in strictPluginOnlyCustomization strips hooks from every non-plugin source, including the --settings blob both drivers inject worker hooks through. Without the flag such a spawn is refused by host_cannot_spawn, naming the policy file and the offending key. With it, the spawn proceeds, the choice is recorded on the ledger row and logged loudly, and 'running degraded' stays a stated operator decision rather than something discovered later from the silence.
embedding_description: Spawn a new fleet-managed session with a required difficulty_score and selector-issued selection_receipt, writing its lifecycle ledger row before host dispatch. It replays the selector and refuses a tuple that is not the current cheapest capability-clearing answer.
dispatch_policy_guidance: dispatch_kind is required provenance: diagnose, design, review, fix, or infrastructure. difficulty_score and selection_receipt are required; selection_receipt_required and selection_receipt_mismatch refuse before a ledger write. Capability floors and quota state are enforced by the replayed selector, never a dispatch-kind pair allowlist.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: agent_instance_id (the new session's identity), host (the resolved driver), host_ref (the driver's spawn handle), lifecycle_state (the ledger row's current state — 'spawning' on a request still in flight, 'terminated' if the dispatch itself failed synchronously), first_turn_source ('charter' if a lane_charter row was on file for this lane and its text was driven as turn 1, 'fallback' if a fixed bootstrap acknowledgement was driven instead), first_turn_delivered (whether that first-turn send actually succeeded — a driver-channel fault here never blocks the spawn itself), and first_turn_error (non-empty detail when first_turn_delivered is false, empty on success).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: State the new agent_instance_id and which host it was dispatched to. If lifecycle_state is 'terminated', make clear the spawn did NOT succeed — read the error for why, not this field alone. If first_turn_delivered is false, say so explicitly and surface first_turn_error, worded per runner: a Claude watch-transport worker with no delivered first turn cannot arm its Stop-hook wake loop; a managed Codex worker has no Stop-hook wake loop to arm at all (stock Codex does not execute async command hooks) and depends on its host driver / drive_on_delivery instead. Either way, first_turn_delivered=false means the worker stays unreachable at zero token cost until someone drives it manually.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validation runs BEFORE the ledger write (unknown_role_class, unknown_work_class, budget_line_required, role_not_legislated, role_class_conflict, reserved_role_name, local_name_already_held) so a refused spawn never touches state. Host resolution errors (host_not_declared, host_mechanism_missing) also precede the write. host_cannot_spawn is the one failure that happens AFTER the ledger row exists — the row is transitioned straight to 'terminated' before the error surfaces, so no spawn is ever left stuck in 'spawning' for a dispatch already known to have failed. local_name_already_held names the incumbent and the terminate_session call that frees the name; the fix is to terminate the holder and re-spawn, never to add a suffix (the mutation guard's compare is exact, so a suffixed name silently loses the capability the spawn was for). host_cannot_spawn also carries the managed-policy refusal: when the host's managed Claude Code policy lists 'hooks' in strictPluginOnlyCustomization, the worker's hooks cannot run and the spawn is refused by name rather than producing a worker that answers turns while never registering. Set degraded_hooks_acknowledged to proceed anyway; it is recorded on the row.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: unknown_role_class/unknown_work_class: the caller passed a value outside the declared taxonomy. budget_line_required: budget_line was empty. role_not_legislated: role_class='principal' named a role_name with no existing role row — principal offices are fill-never-mint, not mintable through this verb. role_class_conflict: role_name already exists under a DIFFERENT role_class than requested. reserved_role_name: role_name matches the <solet>-Main pattern and has no legislated row yet. host_not_declared: an explicit blank host override was passed. host_mechanism_missing: the resolved host (override, FLEET_SESSION_HOST env, or the 'headless' default) has no driver registered in this build at all — none of 'operator'/'headless'/'tmux' matched, most likely a typo'd host name. host_cannot_spawn: the resolved driver is registered but cannot spawn right now — the 'operator' driver never spawns (degenerate by design), or the 'headless'/'tmux' driver is registered but unconfigured (missing permission mode / .mcp.json / the claude binary, or for tmux an unsupported tmux version — the error names exactly which).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For role_not_legislated, legislate the office first via plugin::agent_messaging_plugin::legislate_role (role_class='principal'), or spawn with role_class='project' instead. For host_mechanism_missing, pass a host name that is actually registered ('operator', 'headless', or 'tmux') — there is no other name to wait for; check for a typo. For host_cannot_spawn against 'headless' or 'tmux', fix the exact configuration gap the error names (permission mode, MCP config, the claude binary, or the tmux binary/version); against 'operator', launch the session manually instead — this verb cannot do it for that driver.
